evals.prompt: Build a registration form page using @lifesg/react-design-system v4. The form should collect: full name, email, phone number, and date of birth. Include field validation — all fields required, email must be valid format. Show an error summary at the top if submission fails. Show a success Alert after successful submission. Include Navbar and Footer.
evals.expected_output: A React component using ThemeProvider from @lifesg/react-design-system/theme, Navbar, Footer, Layout.Container type=grid, Form.Input for name/email/phone, Form.DateInput for DOB, Button.Default type=submit with loading+disabled during async, Alert type=error for summary, Alert type=success after submission. errorMessage only set after validation fails. No raw <input> elements. No styled-components. No Tailwind.

assertions.description: Uses Form.DateInput for date of birth
Uses Alert type=error for validation summary
Submit button uses both loading and disabled during async
Does not import styled-components in v4

evals.prompt: Build a service listing page using @lifesg/react-design-system v4. Show a hero banner with a title and a search bar (location input + category dropdown + Search button). Below the hero, show a filter sidebar on the left (sort by radio buttons, category checkboxes) and a results area on the right with a result count and 3 placeholder Card components. Include Navbar and Footer.
evals.expected_output: A React component with Navbar, a hero section, Layout.Container, a two-column layout with Filter component on the left and results on the right. Results area shows Typography.BodyMD for count and Card components. Uses Form.Input for location, Form.Select for category, RadioButton for sort, Filter.Checkbox or Checkbox for categories. No DataTable for citizen-facing results.

assertions.description: Uses Card for citizen-facing results, not DataTable
Does not use DataTable for citizen-facing listing
Shows a result count using Typography

evals.prompt: I need a delete confirmation modal using @lifesg/react-design-system v4. A button labelled 'Delete item' opens a modal. The modal has a title 'Delete this item?', a description 'This action cannot be undone.', a Cancel button and a red Confirm button. Clicking either closes the modal.
evals.expected_output: Uses Modal + Modal.Box with show controlled by useState. enableOverlayClick + onOverlayClick both call the same close handler. Modal.Box has showCloseButton and onClose. Direct child of Modal is not a Fragment. Confirm button uses danger prop. Both Cancel and Confirm call setShow(false).

assertions.description: Does not use Fragment as direct child of Modal
Overlay click handled via enableOverlayClick + onOverlayClick

evals.prompt: Build a dashboard page using @lifesg/react-design-system v4. Show 4 KPI metric cards in a responsive grid (2 columns on tablet, 4 on desktop). Each card shows a metric label, a large number value, and a percentage change badge. Below the cards, show a full-width section heading and a placeholder for a chart. Include Navbar and Footer.
evals.expected_output: Uses Layout.Container type=grid with Layout.ColDiv xsCols=8 mdCols=6 lgCols=3 for the 4-column responsive grid. Metric values use Typography.HeadingXL or similar large heading. Badge component for percentage change. Colour tokens used, not hardcoded hex. No Tailwind classes.

assertions.description: ColDiv uses xsCols for mobile stacking
ColDiv uses lgCols for 4-column desktop layout
Does not hardcode hex colour values
Does not use Tailwind class names

evals.prompt: I need to show a 'no results found' state on my listing page using @lifesg/react-design-system. The search returned zero results. Show the appropriate empty state with a 'Clear filters' action button.
evals.expected_output: Uses ErrorDisplay component with type='no-item-found'. Imports from @lifesg/react-design-system/error-display. Provides actionButton prop with children='Clear filters' and onClick handler. Does not build a custom empty state with raw Typography + Button.

assertions.description: Uses ErrorDisplay component, not a custom empty state
Includes actionButton prop for clear filters

evals.prompt: Add a loading state to my page. While data is fetching, show a full-page loading spinner centred in a card. Once loaded, show the content.
evals.expected_output: Uses LoadingSpinner imported from @lifesg/react-design-system/animations (not invented or from another library). Wrapped in a Card with centred layout. Conditional render based on isLoading state.

assertions.description: Does not invent a custom spinner with raw CSS

evals.prompt: Build a registration form using @lifesg/react-design-system v3. Collect full name, email, and a date of birth. On submit, show a success Toast. Include Navbar and Footer.
evals.expected_output: Uses StyleSheetManager + ThemeProvider with a theme object (e.g. LifeSGTheme) from @lifesg/react-design-system/theme. Uses styled-components for custom layout. Form.Input for name/email. Form.DateInput for DOB. Toast component for success feedback. No raw <input> elements. No plain CSS variables — tokens are interpolation functions inside styled templates.

assertions.description: ThemeProvider receives a theme object, not a string
Uses Form.DateInput for date of birth
Does not use plain CSS variable strings (v4 pattern) in styled-components

evals.prompt: Build a Form.Select dropdown using @lifesg/react-design-system v4. The options are country objects: { value: 'sg', label: 'Singapore' }, { value: 'my', label: 'Malaysia' }. When the user selects an option, the closed selector should show the country name (e.g. 'Singapore'), not the code (e.g. 'sg').
evals.expected_output: Form.Select with options array, valueExtractor returning opt.value, listExtractor returning opt.label, and displayValueExtractor returning opt.label. Without displayValueExtractor the selector shows the raw value ('sg') instead of the label. All three extractors must be present.

assertions.description: Provides displayValueExtractor to show label not raw value in closed selector
displayValueExtractor returns the label field, not value

evals.prompt: I need a read-only summary table showing 3 rows of data: Name, Status, and Date. No sorting or row selection needed. Use @lifesg/react-design-system.
evals.expected_output: Uses Table.Container wrapping Table with Table.Head, Table.Body, Table.Row, Table.HeaderCell and Table.Cell sub-components. Imports from @lifesg/react-design-system/table. Does not use DataTable (overkill for read-only data). Does not use raw <table> HTML.

assertions.description: Wraps table in Table.Container for scroll behaviour
Imports Table from the table subpath
Does not use DataTable for a simple read-only table
Does not use raw <table> HTML elements

evals.prompt: Add a back arrow icon and a settings gear icon to a page header using @lifesg/react-design-system. The back arrow should be on the left, the gear on the right.
evals.expected_output: Imports icons from @lifesg/react-icons subpaths: ArrowLeftIcon from @lifesg/react-icons/arrow-left and GearIcon from @lifesg/react-icons/gear. Does not import from @lifesg/react-design-system directly for icons. Does not use MUI icons when react-icons has a suitable match. Icon component names end in 'Icon'.

assertions.description: Imports from @lifesg/react-icons, not the main DS package
Uses a named arrow icon (not a custom SVG)
Icon component names end in Icon suffix
Does not inline a custom <svg> instead of using the package

evals.prompt: I have a form with a Yes/No question 'Do you agree to the terms?' and a filter panel with a 'Remember me' tick-box. Which DS components should I use for each? Use @lifesg/react-design-system v4.
evals.expected_output: Yes/No question in a form: use Toggle with type='yes' and type='no' (not RadioButton, not Checkbox). Filter tick-box: use Checkbox (not Toggle). Toggle is for card-style form selections; Checkbox is for compact boolean filter/table use.

assertions.description: Uses Toggle for the yes/no form question
Uses Checkbox for the compact filter tick-box
Does not use RadioButton for the binary yes/no question
